title: RBAC v2: guard Dedicated capacity admin endpoints (autoscaling + GPU pool config) behind new permissions
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary: This PR adds RBAC v2 permission checks to Dedicated capacity admin endpoints that mutate autoscaling policies and GPU pool configuration. The checks are enforced behind a rollout flag so we can safely ramp in Hosted/Dedicated control plane without breaking existing enterprise workflows. Motivation: Dedicated customers expect separation of duties (e.g., billing admin != infra admin). Today these endpoints are protected by coarse org-admin gates and some inconsistent console-only checks. As part of RBAC v2, we need explicit permissions for high-impact infra actions and consistent enforcement at the service boundary. What’s included: - New RBAC v2 actions for Dedicated capacity admin operations (see “New actions” below). - Service-side enforcement for Dedicated admin routes (create/update/delete autoscaling policies; create/update/delete GPU pools; update pool sizing/limits; attach/detach pools to capacity reservations). - Rollout flag: rbac_v2_dedicated_admin_enforce (default off) with "shadow" logging to measure would-deny events prior to enforcement. - Standardized 403 error reason codes for these endpoints (maps to console UX messaging) and structured authz logs with actor/org/project + action + resource_id + decision. - Unit tests for policy evaluation wiring + integration tests for least-privilege behavior (Developer cannot mutate; Org Admin can; Support impersonation path explicitly excluded and still requires break-glass session). New actions (names follow ENG-5383 conventions): - dedicated.autoscalingPolicies.read - dedicated.autoscalingPolicies.write - dedicated.gpuPools.read - dedicated.gpuPools.write - dedicated.capacityReservations.attachPool (scoped to reservation_id) Notes on roles: - No default role changes in this PR (policy bundle updates are tracked separately). This PR only introduces actions + enforcement hooks. - During rollout we will temporarily allow Org Admin to continue as before; custom roles can be used once policy bundle v0.1.1 is deployed. Rollout plan: 1) Land with enforcement flag OFF; shadow mode logs would-deny with reason_code=shadow_deny. 2) Enable for internal dogfood orgs + one Dedicated canary (Ops-approved). 3) Expand to 10% Dedicated orgs, monitor 403 spikes + console error feedback. 4) Full enable once policy bundle changes are confirmed in rbac-policy-bundle. Testing: - Added integration test coverage for dedicated-admin router guards. - Verified console flows in staging: autoscaling policy edit; GPU pool resize; attach pool to reservation. - Benchmarked overhead: authz evaluation p95 +0.25ms for these routes; cache hit >99% in staging. Follow-ups: - Add read-only guards to list/get endpoints for Dedicated admin screens (tracked in ENG-5401). - Console: permission-aware disabling of buttons + better inline messaging (DES-241).

conversation:
Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Can we confirm we’re not only relying on console-side checks? We need service enforcement for Private control planes too.
Benji Okafor (author): Yep — checks are in dedicatedadmin service handlers. Console will get UX updates separately; Private uses the same control-plane codepath when running in customer VPC.

Ethan Park (review): What’s the resource scoping here? These endpoints are org-wide; do we have reservation/pool IDs in the resource to avoid over-broad grants?
Benji Okafor (author): For gpuPools.* actions we scope to gpu_pool_id. For attach/detach we scope to reservation_id (and include pool_id in log fields). Read/write actions are still org-scoped via policy but evaluation gets the concrete IDs for auditability.

Sean Gallagher (review): Break-glass: do we need to make sure on-call tooling still works during incidents? Some of our runbooks hit these endpoints.
Benji Okafor (author): Enforcement is behind rbac_v2_dedicated_admin_enforce, default off. Shadow logs will tell us which on-call actors would be denied. Also, break-glass elevated sessions remain allowed (separate check) — but still audited.

Naomi Feldman (PM review): Which default roles will get these permissions? Concerned that Billing Admin currently manages Dedicated settings in a few customers.
Benji Okafor (author): Not changing defaults in this PR. Policy bundle will likely grant dedicated.*.read to Billing Admin (for visibility) but not write. For the handful of customers who want billing to adjust autoscaling, we’ll recommend a custom role. I’ll add a note to the rollout doc.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (request changes): Please add integration tests for 403 reason_code stability (console relies on it) and ensure shadow mode does not emit 403.
Benji Okafor (author): Added tests asserting (1) enforcement returns 403 with reason_code=insufficient_permissions and action name, (2) shadow mode returns 200 but logs shadow_deny. Pushed in 8c3b1a9.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (approve): LGTM after latest changes. Thanks for including shadow metrics.
Ethan Park (approve): Approved.
Sean Gallagher (approve): Approved with note to coordinate rollout with SRE.
